stories.headline: Henderson's Ankle Keeps Him Off the Range Again, and the Whole Saloon Is Holdin' Its Breath
stories.read: Hold up there, pardner. TreVeyon Henderson slipped on a cut Monday, tweaked that right ankle, and sat out again Tuesday with no clearance to run. Now the word from folks who'd know is he dodged anything serious and oughta be good to go when New England rides into Seattle on the ninth. Here's the play: if some jumpy greenhorn in your outfit lets the best young back on the board slide half a round over a two-day scare, you smile polite and take him. That's a gold vein gettin' priced like gravel.

stories.headline: Dallas Cleans Out the Corral, and Javonte Williams Is Suddenly Holdin' All the Reins
stories.read: Well now, the Cowboys cut Jaydon Blue loose Sunday, sent Phil Mafah down the road too, then claimed Emari Demercado off the Kansas City scrap heap Monday just to have a body who can block. Read what that actually says: nobody in that barn is takin' carries away from Javonte Williams. Schottenheimer wanted pass protection, not a rival, and a fella who gets the ball twenty times beats a genius who gets it five. Williams is goin' at a price the saloon set back when they thought this was a committee. Go stake that claim before the herd catches on.

stories.headline: Chicago Names Two Tight Ends Starters, Which Is Frontier Talk for Nobody Eats Full
stories.read: The Bears rolled out their pecking order for the opener against Carolina and there sit Colston Loveland AND Cole Kmet, both listed as starters, both fixin' to be on the field together in them two-tight sets. Loveland's the No. 1 and he's the strike I still like, but split kitchens serve thin soup, and Kmet at his current price is a dry well dressed up as a starter. Meanwhile Ben Johnson keeps sayin' D'Andre Swift is primed for a big year, which tells you where the money patch touches are headed. Ride Loveland late, let some other fella pay up for Kmet's job title.
